verdicts.evidence: Hole, measured 2026-11-04 (anchor `^` removed). MISSION_CONTRACT_TITLE is read only by declaredMissionName, whose value is the in-toto subject name and predicate `mission` of `check --attest`, the VSA subject, the bundle predicate, the OSCAL seed and the JUnit payload digest; `check --strict --json` does not carry it, which is why mutation-probe.mjs (json only) reports no observable difference on every fixture for this regex (run on `t-h2` and `t-nosp`: 0/4), and why the attestation was compared. Fixtures: `base` (`# Mission Contract: Inbound Request Triage`), `t-h2` (`## Mission Contract: ...`), `t-2sp` (two spaces after `#`), `t-nosp` (no space after the colon), `t-tab` (tabs), `t-nbsp` and `t-lead-nbsp` (a no-break space after/before the name), `t-empty` (`# Mission Contract:` with no name), `t-none` (no such heading), `t-brk` (`[Triage] inbound requests`), `t-ph` (`[Name of the system]`). Observed: `t-h2` attestation subject name "mission" (pristine: an H2 is not the contract title) -> "Inbound Request Triage" (the mutant matches from the second `#`). The other ten fixtures identical. A machine output that names what was attested changes on a constructible contract, and nothing kills it. Recipe (2026-11-04, measurement of CI run 41823714837 on main a3a614f; dist/lib/mission.js SHA-256 equal to the source embedded in the report): fixture missions made with `runward init --example` (scaffold-lock carries structureContract:true) in a scratch directory outside any git tree, each changed in exactly one file as named below; the mutant applied by exact offset into dist/lib/mission.js, read back, and `check --strict --json`, `check --strict --attest` and the rendered `check --strict` text compared byte-for-byte (exit code and stdout) against the pristine build, pristine run twice to rule out nondeterminism; then the file restored. `scripts/mutation-probe.mjs --function <f> --mission <fixture>` was run as well and its outcome is quoted.
